hints: Run DFS while remembering the parent edge for each vertex.
A visited neighbor other than the parent indicates a cycle in this undirected graph.
Save parents and reconstruct the path from the current vertex through the ancestor back to itself.
analogy: When exploration reaches a previously visited road destination through a different road, it has closed a loop.
example: Edges 1-2,2-3,3-1 form a cycle; output the vertices around it and repeat the first at the end.
algorithm: DFS with states and parent pointers. On a back edge to an active ancestor, trace parents to that ancestor, reverse the chain, and append the ancestor again.
correctness: The back edge plus the unique DFS-tree path between its endpoints forms a cycle; every reported consecutive pair is an input edge.
